quotes.text: Beijing has also deployed facial--as you pointed out, Mr. Chairman--and voice recognition, artificial intelligence and other surveillance technologies throughout the country but particularly targeting the Uyghur ethnic minority where between 500,000 and a million Uyghurs have been detained arbitrarily.

In so doing, Xi is able to draw upon technology, the likes of which the Mao Zedongs could only dream of, from artificial intelligence, to tracking apps, which bring us closer than ever before to the nightmare envisioned by George Orwell.

Chinese authorities' relentless persecution of predominantly Muslim Uyghurs, Kazakhs, and other Central Asian people in the country's Xinjiang region provides a disturbing preview of these tools' misuse on an even broader scale.
The CCP bombards Taiwan with propaganda and false narratives, seeking to manipulate the information space, including through the use of “deep fake” video clips created using artificial intelligence.

Taiwan’s investments will also help advance U.S. energy and artificial intelligence production, creating countless jobs and bolstering our economy. [...] At a critical moment when the United States and Communist China are locked in a tight race for technological dominance, Taiwan’s impressive investment in U.S. technological development makes a world of difference.
AI data centers pose critical environmental risks and impose undue stresses on local resources—including water and electricity—which place significant financial burdens on ratepayers and residents.

The people who will have to endure the negative consequences of data center development in their communities deserve to have their voices heard. The reasonable concerns of local residents must no longer be steamrolled by tech companies seeking profit over Americans’ quality of life—not on my watch.

The Ratepayer Protection Act will inject transparency and public scrutiny into the system to ensure that the largest users of energy—including hyperscale data centers—pay for energy infrastructure upgrades and generation capacity. [...] American families deserve protection from exorbitant and unpredictable energy bills, and this legislation ensures that the companies who want to build and operate data centers will be made to pay for the massive amounts of electricity they consume.
